latest_nl_proof: Work in the rational-function field in q. By definition, [n choose r]_q = (prod_{i=1}^r (1 - q^(n-r+i))) / (prod_{i=1}^r (1 - q^i)), and, replacing r by n-r, [n choose n-r]_q = (prod_{i=1}^{n-r} (1 - q^(r+i))) / (prod_{i=1}^{n-r} (1 - q^i)). Set A = prod_{i=1}^r (1 - q^(n-r+i)), B = prod_{i=1}^r (1 - q^i), C = prod_{i=1}^{n-r} (1 - q^i), and D = prod_{i=1}^{n-r} (1 - q^(r+i)). Then [n choose r]_q = A/B and [n choose n-r]_q = D/C. The factors in A are exactly (1 - q^t) for t = n-r+1, ..., n, while the factors in C are exactly (1 - q^t) for t = 1, ..., n-r. These two index sets are disjoint and their union is {1, ..., n}; hence, by commutativity of multiplication, A C = prod_{t=1}^n (1 - q^t). Similarly, the factors in D are exactly (1 - q^t) for t = r+1, ..., n, while the factors in B are exactly (1 - q^t) for t = 1, ..., r, so again the index sets are disjoint with union {1, ..., n}; hence D B = prod_{t=1}^n (1 - q^t). Therefore A C = D B. Now B and C are nonzero (each is a finite product of factors 1 - q^i, or an empty product equal to 1), so in the rational-function field we may divide by B C and obtain A/B = D/C. Thus [n choose r]_q = [n choose n-r]_q. This includes the boundary cases r = 0 and r = n, since the relevant empty product is 1.
role_in_parent: Reduces the original quotient to the symmetric indices a := min(k, n-k) and b := min(l, n-l).
statement_nl: For integers n and r with 0 <= r <= n, define the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient by [n choose r]_q := prod_{i=1}^r (1 - q^(n-r+i)) / (1 - q^i), with the empty product equal to 1 when r = 0. Then [n choose r]_q = [n choose n-r]_q.

domain_restrictions: The product index i ranges over integers i = 1,2,...,r; when r = 0 the product is empty and equals 1

Implicitly, the denominator factors (1 - q^i) for i = 1,...,r must be meaningful (nonzero) if q is a numeric parameter; alternatively the identity is intended in a formal/polynomial/rational-function sense where the expression is well-defined
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For all integers n and r with 0 <= r <= n, the quantity defined by [n choose r]_q := (∏_{i=1}^r (1 - q^(n-r+i)))/(∏_{i=1}^r (1 - q^i)), with ∏_{i=1}^0 := 1, satisfies [n choose r]_q = [n choose (n-r)]_q, where [n choose (n-r)]_q is defined by the same formula with r replaced by (n-r).
quantifier_order: with 0 <= r <= n: define [n choose r]_q by the given product (empty product convention when r = 0); then assert equality [n choose r]_q = [n choose n-r]_q
